function: Transceiver design for over-the-air federated distillation: closed-form WD transmit power and estimator, plus receiver beamforming by semidefinite relaxation, minimizing a convergence bound of soft-prediction aggregation (pp. 3-6).
system: Uplink over-the-air aggregation: PS with N=5 antennas, M=50 single-antenna devices, 915 MHz, block fading, perfect CSI at PS; no RIS (pp. 3-4, 6).
method: Federated distillation: ResNet-18 trained by gradient descent on per-class soft predictions aggregated over the air; transceiver by closed form and SDR, no learned transceiver (pp. 2-6).
data_channel: Own channel: IID Gaussian small-scale fading times free-space path loss, exponent 4; FMNIST and CIFAR-10 for the learning task, IID and Dirichlet non-IID partitions (pp. 6-7).
test_conditions: Train/test split of the same dataset; sweeps over PS antennas, distillation weight and CSI error; IID and non-IID partitions; no cross-condition test stated (pp. 6-8).
baselines: Error-free FD and FedAvg, uniform beamforming, orthogonal channels, and earlier over-the-air designs: MSE minimization [11], 90%-sparse rate [9], 80% pruning with QAT [15] (p. 8).
metrics: Global average testing accuracy, analytical convergence gap, training and distillation loss, eigenvalues of the SDR solution, uplink communication time, overall time consumption (pp. 7-9).
complexity: Algorithm 1 costs O(N^3 + M) per FD round (SDR O(N^3), eigendecomposition O(N^2.376)); average run time 0.12 s per round (p. 6).
q1_support: p. 6: "The channel coefficient is modelled by the small scale fading multiplied by the square root of the path loss." IID Gaussian fading with free-space path loss, exponent 4: a custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel is named.
q2_support: p. 6: "The FMNIST dataset consists of 60000 28 × 28 grayscale training images in K = 10 classes and 10000 testing images." Testing uses the held-out split of the same data; the antenna and CSI-error sweeps (pp. 7-8) are sweeps, and no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 9: "the proposed algorithm achieves a higher performance than the MSE minimization benchmark"; MSE minimization [11], 90%-sparse rate [9] and pruning with QAT [15] are earlier over-the-air designs, and uniform beamforming is the non-learned baseline (p. 8).
q4_support: p. 6: "the average run time per round of Algorithm 1 is 0.12s"; Section IV-B gives the transceiver design cost as O(N^3 + M) per FD round.
q5_support: p. 6: "We simulate an image classification task on ResNet-18 over the FMNIST and CIFAR-10 dataset." Public datasets of the learning task alone do not count; no code or data link and no channel dataset is stated anywhere in the paper.
notes: Preprint arXiv:2507.15256v1, titled 'Optimal Transceiver Design in Over-the-Air Federated Distillation'; the DOI cannot be checked against the title from the PDF alone. Area 7: the problem is over-the-air aggregation of soft predictions, solved by closed-form power control and SDR receive beamforming (pp. 4-6), not by a learned transceiver. Included because federated learning over the air passes the learning check, the learned element being the model trained across devices (ResNet-18, p. 6). Multi-antenna PS (p. 3), so the system check passes. RIS appears only in a reference title (ref. [29]), so ris is 0. q3 relies on the rule that earlier published over-the-air designs count as the learned baseline; reviewer to confirm.
